Native/mock tests and compilation did not exercise these actual retained schemas.

remaining_blockers.preparation_impact: Current run_non_delete provisions new disabled source IAM before restored business trial. The trial is not runnable against the frozen old schema; do not allocate the candidate86 owners or reach PROVISION merely because source unit review passed.
remaining_blockers.dispatch_impact: Even an existing persisted plan requires GetPlan/LoadFixtureCopies on real sender/reconciliation paths; replay does not avoid the column dependency.

prior_review.interpretation: Prior PASS records the checks and unit/mock facts evaluated then. This append-only new finding supersedes any allocation/readiness inference; it does not rewrite prior test outcomes or evidence.

finite_design_recommendation: First restore each existing hash-bound core.dump into a NEW isolated PostgreSQL instance/volume using existing pg_restore tooling and fixed image, without starting any source Core/native or old owner. This produces only compatibility evidence and cannot substitute for authoritative source acceptance.

Read the actual ordered schema_migration version/name set from the restored copy and compare it with the fixed migration-file set. The fingerprint rows=66 is only a row count: the dumps already contain policy-renewal/reference-guard DDL. Do not infer version66, preselect 67-71, hand-edit migration metadata or ignore duplicate/partial DDL.

On the unmodified restored copy, execute the actual current repository LoadFixtureCopies/GetPlan path to retain the missing-column error before any provider invocation. Then let the existing official migration Runner apply only its actually pending versions on the copy; retain exact Runner input/output/failure facts.

Positive copy evidence must show current repository loads all 17 expected exact-provider-version identities and frozen plan hashes, protected objects remain ineligible for exact disposal, old-column projections/immutable facts/pins/attempts/costs remain unchanged, and provider DELETE/calls stay zero. Any migration failure or partial schema stays BLOCKED.

If the same six physical targets must continue using their original source Core, prepare a separate explicit bounded source-schema maintenance proposal with backup/known Core identities/expected DDL+data delta, Runner versions, privilege/containment and acceptance steps. Source migration is outside current no-migration preparation contract and must not be inferred from old deletion authorization or from copy PASS.

After any separately authorized source maintenance, capture a NEW current Core baseline and new native/non-delete evidence, retaining every old baseline/dump/raw hash. Full fingerprints are expected to change for schema additions; preserve old-column/value facts and old scope hashes rather than falsely reporting source fingerprint unchanged. New candidate/final CI/native branch lock/new exact authorization remain required.

If source schema must remain unchanged, this current binary/source cannot execute the same source-backed remaining-six plan. Keep it blocked. Do not delete the identity_kind predicate, weaken protected-object guards, silently choose an old binary/authority, or treat a migrated clone as the original Core.
